slot.brief: Flow/sequence: start with a calcium compound, follow thermal decomposition and water reaction steps; identify the intermediates and final product in the lime–water cycle.

stem: On heating $\text{CaCO}_3$, it forms $X+Y$; $X$ reacts with water to give $Z$, and limited $\text{CO}_2$ converts $Z$ to $W$. Identify $X,Y,Z,W$.

verdicts.working: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂; CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂. Limited CO₂ converts Ca(OH)₂ to CaCO₃, so option B.

working:
$\text{CaCO}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} \text{CaO}+\text{CO}_2$; hence $X=\text{CaO},\ Y=\text{CO}_2$.\n$\text{CaO}+\text{H}_2\text{O}\to\text{Ca(OH)}_2$; $\text{Ca(OH)}_2+\text{CO}_2\to\text{CaCO}_3+\text{H}_2\text{O}$.

Independent check: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂; CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂. Limited CO₂ converts Ca(OH)₂ to CaCO₃, so option B.
solution:
On heating, calcium carbonate undergoes thermal decomposition:
$$\text{CaCO}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} \text{CaO}+\text{CO}_2$$
Then $\text{CaO}+\text{H}_2\text{O}\to\text{Ca(OH)}_2$, and limited $\text{CO}_2$ gives $\text{Ca(OH)}_2+\text{CO}_2\to\text{CaCO}_3+\text{H}_2\text{O}$. Thus $X=\text{CaO},\ Y=\text{CO}_2,\ Z=\text{Ca(OH)}_2,\ W=\text{CaCO}_3$..

draft.distractor_notes: A: gives CO instead of CO₂ on heating.\nC: forms bicarbonate, which requires excess CO₂.\nD: reverses the oxide and hydroxide steps.
